title: Solo developer buying an API
instance: Oct 13: the minimum-party case. Adrian [00:39:45] “That's the minimum number of parties in this, and that single developer is both the principal and the buyer.” Oct 27: the Principal and Buyer lanes are drawn as one person.
lanes: principal and buyer in one person

A.label: none to delegate: the developer is principal and buyer
A.sub: identity: the developer · delegated authority: none, the developer spends its own funds · audit trail: the developer's own records

A2.label: the developer sets the agent's scope
A2.sub: which API, how much, for how long

B.label: this seller's profile: an email, self-attested
B.sub: the 402 carries the payment terms and, via extensions, the ask for an email · the answer: M3 signature + authorization.from, the email alongside · another seller may set a different profile

C.label: the wallet address is the identifier anchor
C.sub: authorization.from · the same address across calls · says which account, not which person

C2.label: no identity link asked for
C2.sub: 4.2.1 is at the Principal's election; this seller's profile does not need it

E.label: the developer reviews its own spend
E.sub: no Verifier or Relying Party beyond the developer

differs: Differs from K0 in A (collapses: principal = buyer, one lane) and in B (this seller’s profile asks for one self-attested field).
slots: The developer is both principal and buyer; the agent spends the developer’s own funds. In Nicole’s three-way split (Oct 27 00:32–00:36) the identity is the developer, the delegated authority is empty, and the audit trail is the developer’s own records. Adrian [00:39:31] “perhaps they've got loaded their own wallet with stablecoins and they want to use X402 to experiment with it.”
This seller’s profile: an email, self-attested

The lowest profile a seller can set, not a universal minimum. Adrian [00:39:50] “perhaps the API vendor might want an email or something to know who's using their service.” A seller fighting free-trial abuse would set the assurance dial higher (Nicole, Oct 27 00:40).
The wallet address is the identifier anchor
The spec’s only identifier. Metering and the free tier key off it. It names an account, not a person (Adrian, Oct 27).
The developer reviews its own spend
No auditor, no dispute evaluator. Limit evidence is the developer’s own concern.
footer: Nicole [00:26:39]: “a developer buying an API service, which is a core use case of Explorer 2 [x402] today.” Works with no identity at all.
An email in B, keyed to the wallet in C. Nothing else.

Whether x402 should recommend a universal minimum profile (Nicole, Oct 27 00:37–00:42: “potentially” a requirement, not the diagram) · whether this case needs a diagram of its own or is the empty instance of K0 (Adrian [00:39:55]: “the simplest place to start with”).
